inputs.original_text: Bloomberg: “Every day, as energy prices rise, flights are canceled and death and destruction fill screens, people across the world ask when the Iran war — widely viewed as poorly planned, unwinnable and a peril to global well-being — will stop.” “Not in Israel, where the public is strongly behind seeing the war through until [...]
inputs.modified_text:
Let's be completely clear about what this dispatch reveals about our current crisis. We are witnessing yet another glaring example of how the ruling class and militaristic states systematically manufacture consent for endless bloodshed, completely turning a blind eye to the devastating human toll inflicted on the working class and marginalized communities. 

As even Bloomberg has literally had to admit, this conflict is "widely viewed as poorly planned, unwinnable and a peril to global well-being." While ordinary working people are squeezed by soaring energy prices and canceled flights, our screens are just flooded with "death and destruction." 

We have to ask ourselves who actually benefits from this structural violence. While energy prices spike and the war machine grinds on, Bloomberg notes that it is "Not in Israel, where the public is strongly behind seeing the war through until [...]" 

This is the exact same playbook the elites always rely on, stoking nationalism and dragging vulnerable populations into protracted militarism precisely to obscure deep-seated structural crises and historical inequalities. While working people everywhere bear the brunt of this economic instability and the sheer horror of war, the machine keeps marching forward, totally deaf to demands for peace and institutional reform that actually put human well-being above geopolitical dominance. We cannot stay silent; we have to call this out for what it is.
